title: Guest Bath and Dresser Vanity
summary: A compact old-house bath was brought back into service around an antique dresser adapted as a vessel-sink vanity.
searchSummary: Guest bath restoration with retained beadboard, tile, windows, and clawfoot tub, centered on fitting plumbing and a vessel sink into an antique dresser vanity.
sourceLabel: Guest bath restoration journal and Home Reno - Guest Bath Flickr album

gallery.caption: The room back in use with the dresser vanity, vessel sink, mirror, lighting, beadboard, windows, tile, and tub working together.
The antique dresser was finished and prepared before receiving the sink and plumbing.
Low-profile clamping and careful fitting made the vessel sink part of the dresser rather than a loose addition.

introduction: A small bathroom concentrates a surprising number of trades into one room. The central craft problem here was adapting an antique dresser for modern plumbing and a vessel sink while keeping the retained fabric of the room visually intact.
evidenceBoundary: The selected evidence documents surface repair, vanity preparation, sink fitting, and the room returned to use. It does not support claims about unseen plumbing, wiring, waterproofing, or code compliance.
